gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order from the repo root, then share the resulting report(s)/logs if you want help interpreting or deciding what to promote.

## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module selection + best pick)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for after it finishes:
- Which module/candidate it promoted (if any)
- Any failures/timeouts
- Where it wrote the comparison report (often under `baseline/reports/` or an experiment output dir)

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for:
- Any system candidate that beats `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- Whether results are PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE and why (metric deltas, confidence, minimums, etc.)

## 3) Generate “next fix” guidance
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
Then open:
```bash
sed -n '1,200p' baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

## If you paste back anything, paste these
- The tail of each command output (last ~50–100 lines)
- Any generated summary table/report paths
- Contents (or key sections) of `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

If you tell me what “tuning” and “lockbox” metrics represent (and the PASS criteria, if you have them), I can also help decide whether a candidate should be promoted or whether the run is stuck in a local optimum.
